v1.feedback: The edge-biased particle placement (70% on panel edges) directly embodies limning-as-outlining and the gold-leaf/vellum/ink palette correctly evokes manuscript illumination — the word visibly drove the design. The cornice vault skeleton survives legibly from the parent. Two things to sharpen: the 9-rib radial symmetry with 72 small panels risks reading as a spiky sea-urchin from oblique angles rather than a vaulted ceiling — reduce to 5–6 ribs or vary rib lengths so the silhouette has more directional character. The trace particles (the animated golden sweeps along edges) are the strongest limning gesture but get only ~20k of the budget and compete with the dense static edge particles — give traces higher alpha and larger point size so the illumination act itself dominates the read.

v2.feedback: The limning concept genuinely drove design: 85% edge-concentrated particles act as manuscript outlines, gold/ink/vellum palette is period-correct, and trace particles animate like a limner's brush along vault ribs. Parent cornice architecture is preserved and morphed rather than replaced. Two improvements: increase trace particle brightness or size so the gold edge-tracing reads more dramatically against the dark vellum panels at first glance, and tighten the camera (z=20 is slightly far for a ~9-unit span vault — try z=14) so the gilt structure fills more frame area and the outlining detail is immediately legible.
